rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary places the inspiration to Moses’ mother alongside revelation to bees and prophets, while noting that inspiration can also be attributed to devils addressing their allies.
rows.anchor: وقوله في أم موسى { وأوحينا إلى أم موسى } الآية أو بنحو آخر كما في الأنبياء والرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse compresses the intervening events: Moses’ mother conceived and gave birth amid acute danger, after which God inspired her.
rows.anchor: في الكلام إيجاز بالحذف والتقدير وحبلت أم موسى به - والحال هذه الحال من الشدة والحدة -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She is to nurse Moses while safe from Pharaoh’s discovery; when she fears the family will find and kill him, she must cast him into the Nile, trust that he will return, and know he will become a messenger to Pharaoh and Israel.
rows.anchor: من قبل فرعون فإذا خفت عليه - أن يطلع عليه آل فرعون فيأخذوه ويقتلوه - فألقيه في البحر وهو النيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to return Moses explains the prohibition against grieving, as the later account says his mother received him back so her eye might be comforted and she would not grieve.
rows.anchor: فقوله { إنا رادوه إليك } تعليل للنهي في قوله { ولا تحزني } كما يشهد به أيضا قوله بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear concerns a harm that may occur, whereas grief concerns a harm whose occurrence is certain.
rows.anchor: الفرق بين الخوف والحزن بحسب المورد أن الخوف إنما يكون في مكروه محتمل الوقوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iltqāṭ is finding and taking something without having sought it; al-yamm is the sea or a large river, and ilqāʾ is casting or throwing.
rows.anchor: إصابة الشيء وأخذه من غير طلب، ومنه اللقطة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed reported grammatical view takes the lām in “so that he would be an enemy and grief” as a lām of eventual outcome.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله { ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا } للعاقبة - على ما قيل -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grief denotes its cause, a figurative intensification of how strongly Moses would cause their grief; ḥazan and ḥuzn mean the same thing.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالحزن سبب الحزن فإطلاق الحزن عليه مبالغة في سببيته لحزنهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāṭiʾ describes someone who intends an act he does not do well and performs it; mukhṭiʾ describes someone who intends a fitting act but ends up doing something else.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين الخاطئ والمخطئ على ما ذكره الراغب أن الخاطئ يطلق على من أراد فعلا لا يحسنه

words: ونريد أن نمن على الذين استضعفوا في الأرض
rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn Abī Shayba, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim says ʿAlī identified the oppressed people as Joseph and his descendants.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب رضى الله عنه في قوله تعالى { ونريد أن نمن على الذين استضعفوا في الأرض } قال يوسف وولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabataba’i suggests ʿAlī may have meant the Children of Israel, since the verse’s apparent meaning clearly points elsewhere than Joseph and his descendants.
rows.anchor: أقول لعل المراد بنو إسرائيل، وإلا فظهور الآية في خلافه غير خفي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal reports al-Ṣādiq’s explanation that the Prophet’s description of ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn as oppressed after him means they are the Imams after him, and the verse applies to them until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن سنان عن المفضل بن عمر قال سمعت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام يقول إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Numerous Shiʿi reports identify the verse with the Imams of the Prophet’s household; Tabataba’i classifies these as continuing applications, as this report indicates.
rows.anchor: والروايات من طرق الشيعة في كون الآية في أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام كثيرة وبهذه الرواية يظهر أنها جميعا من قبيل الجري والانطباق

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Nahj al-Balāgha quotes ʿAlī saying the world will turn back to the Prophet’s family after its resistance, like a nursing camel returning to its young, and then reciting this verse.
rows.anchor: وفي نهج البلاغة لتعطفن الدنيا علينا بعد شماسها عطف الضروس على ولدها وتلا عقيب ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Bāqir reports Pharaoh, warned Moses would destroy him, ordered Israelite boys killed; Moses’ hidden pregnancy ended at birth, an Egyptian attendant consoled his frightened mother, who placed him in an ark and cast him into the Nile, where Pharaoh and Asiya found and loved him.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال إنه لما حملت به أمه لم يظهر حملها إلا عند وضعها له وكان فرعون قد وكل بنساء بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: جل المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes say the Israelite whom Moses had come to help spoke the accusation: frightened by Moses’ anger at his earlier conduct, he feared Moses meant to strike him.
rows.anchor: ذكر جل المفسرين أن ضمير { قال } للإسرائيلي الذي كان يستصرخه وذلك أنه ظن أن موسى إنما يريد

words: أتريد أن تقتلني كما قتلت نفسا بالأمس
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabataba’i accepts the Israelite as speaker on contextual grounds and rejects the claim that the Copt spoke; the Israelite’s words revealed Moses as yesterday’s killer, prompting the Copt to inform Pharaoh and the plot to kill Moses.
rows.anchor: وما ذكروه في محله لشهادة السياق بذلك فلا يعبأ بما قيل إن القائل هو القبطي دون الإسرائيلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Copt an enemy to both men implicitly contradicts the present Torah’s claim that both fighters were Israelites, and supports the Israelite as the speaker.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله { أن يبطش بالذي هو عدو لهما } تعريض للتوراة الحاضرة حيث تذكر أن المتقاتلين هذين كانا جميعا إسرائيليين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʾtimār means consultation, and naṣīḥa (sincere advice) is the opposite of treachery.
rows.anchor: الائتمار المشاورة، والنصيحة خلاف الخيانة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “from the farthest part of the city” grammatically qualifies “came”; the story suggests the conspiracy was at Pharaoh’s order and the man came from there to warn Moses.
rows.anchor: والظاهر كون قوله { من أقصى المدينة } قيدا لقوله { جاء } فسياق القصة يعطي أن الإئتمار كان عند فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inference that the palace Pharaoh lived in stood beyond the city is reinforced by the story’s wording about the man coming from its far end.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاستئناس من الكلام يؤيد ما تقدم أن قصر فرعون الذي كان يسكنه كان خارج المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ flight in fear supports the view that he did not consider the accidental killing of the Copt a crime for which he was culpable.
rows.anchor: فيه تأييد أنه ما كان يرى قتله القبطي خطأ جرما لنفسه

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: A report in Tafsīr al-Qummī says Moses had been honored at Pharaoh’s court until adulthood; after killing Pharaoh’s follower while defending an Israelite, he hid, then fled when another Israelite repeated the accusation.
rows.anchor: فلم يزل موسى عند فرعون في أكرم كرامة حتى بلغ مبلغ الرجال

rows.speaker: علي بن محمد بن الجهم
rows.claim: In a report from the meeting of al-Maʾmūn and al-Riḍā, al-Maʾmūn asks whether al-Riḍā holds that prophets are infallible, and al-Riḍā affirms it.
rows.anchor: بإسناده إلى علي بن محمد بن الجهم قال حضرت مجلس المأمون وعنده الرضا عليه السلام فقال له المأمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that Moses’ teaching is unprecedented among the ancestors does not refute it; the point is that his religion is new to them, not that lack of precedent proves it false.
rows.anchor: على أن عدم معهودية السحر وعدم مسبوقيته بالمثل لا ينفعهم شيئا حتى يدعوه. فالمعنى أن ما جاء به موسى دين مبتدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses answers that the ancestors never heard this teaching: God, Lord of creation and command, knows best who brought guidance and who will attain the final abode; Moses says God sent him with monotheism and signs as proof.
rows.anchor: مقتضى السياق كونه جوابا من موسى عن قولهم { وما سمعنا بهذا في آبائنا الأولين } في رد دعوى موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Whoever brings guidance from Him” refers to Moses himself, and “guidance” means the monotheistic religious call he brought.
rows.anchor: فقوله { ربي أعلم بمن جاء بالهدى من عنده } يريد به نفسه والمراد بالهدى الدعوة الدينية التي جاء بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final abode may mean Paradise, this world’s eventual outcome, or both; Tabataba’i prefers the comprehensive sense, then the worldly sense, supported by the statement that wrongdoers do not prosper.
rows.anchor: المراد بعاقبة الدار إما الجنة التي هي الدار الآخرة التي يسكنها السعداء كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This alludes to Pharaoh and his people and denies their success because they built life on oppression, deviating from social justice aligned with human nature and the cosmic order.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله { إنه لا يفلح الظالمون } تعريض لفرعون وقومه وفيه نفي أن تكون لهم عاقبة الدار

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes say the placement of Moses’ answer beside the opponents’ claim lets hearers compare the statements and distinguish true from false; Tabataba’i prefers a direct reply to their claim about the ancestors.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين والوجه في عطف قوله

words: ما علمت لكم من إله غيري
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh insinuates that Moses’ call and miraculous signs have not convinced him of God’s existence or shown the signs to be divine proofs.
rows.anchor: فيه تعريض لموسى بما جاء به من الدعوة الحقة المؤيدة بالآيات المعجزة يريد أنه لم يتبين له حقية ما يدعو إليه موسى

words: ما علمت لكم من إله غيري
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh casts his claim as fair-minded reasoning so the elite will accept it, as in his other claim that he shows them only what he sees and guides them only to the right path.
rows.anchor: فقوله { ما علمت لكم من إله غيري } سوق للكلام في صورة الإنصاف ليقع في قلوب الملأ موقع القبول

words: ما علمت لكم من إله غيري
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement is a counter-restriction: Moses affirms God’s divinity and denies it of all others, while Pharaoh denies God and claims divinity for himself; other gods worshipped by Pharaoh’s people are not addressed.
rows.anchor: قصر القلب فقد كان موسى عليه السلام يثبت الألوهية لله سبحانه وينفيها عن غيره وهو ينفيها عنه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kindle fire over clay means firing it into bricks for building; a ṣarḥ is a high, exposed structure, from the idea of something becoming visible.
rows.anchor: والصرح البناء العالي المكشوف من صرح الشيء إذا ظهر ففي الجملة أمر باتخاذ الآجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The result is put before its premise: Pharaoh wants a structure to climb high enough to look toward the sky and perhaps see Moses’ God, whom he imagines as a body somewhere in the atmosphere or celestial spheres.
rows.anchor: والكلام من وضع النتيجة موضع المقدمة والتقدير اجعل لي صرحا أصعد إلى أعلى درجاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh’s claim may be deliberate obfuscation meant to mislead the people.
rows.anchor: أو كان هذا القول من قبيل التعمية على الناس وإضلالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that Pharaoh wants an observatory to watch the stars and see whether they indicate a messenger’s mission or the truth of Moses’ description; a parallel wording supports it.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون المراد أن يبني له رصدا يترصد الكواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh escalates from ignorance implied by “I know no god but myself” to suspicion that Moses is lying, which Tabataba’i says is itself a lie intended to confuse the people.
rows.anchor: وقوله { وإني لأظنه من الكاذبين } ترق منه من الجهل

words: ما علمت لكم من إله غيري
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some commentators read this as denying a god through lack of knowledge, implying that a real god would have become evident; Tabataba’i rejects this because it does not fit the verse’s ending.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن قوله { ما علمت لكم من إله غيري } من قبيل نفي المعلوم بنفي العلم فيما لو كان لبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses counters Pharaoh’s false denial by saying he already knows these signs were sent only by the Lord of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: لقد علمت ما أنزل هؤلاء إلا رب السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their apparent expectation that they would not return to God masks an inward certainty, as another verse says they denied the signs despite being inwardly convinced.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى { وجحدوا بها واستيقنتها أنفسهم ظلما وعلوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabdh means casting or throwing, and al-yamm means the sea; the rest of the verse is clear.
rows.anchor: النبذ الطرح، واليم البحر والباقي ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording conveys both contempt for Pharaoh and his troops and the enormity of the punishment that befell them.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية من الاستهانة بأمرهم وتهويل العذاب الواقع بهم ما لا يخفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being made leaders calling to the Fire means they lead in misguidance and are imitated; Fire denotes sins that merit it or is named for their consequence, and their leadership is retribution, not initial divine misguidance.
rows.anchor: ومعنى جعلهم أئمة يدعون إلى النار، تصييرهم سابقين في الضلال يقتدي بهم اللاحقون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says God merely called them leaders, like the verse saying angels were made female; Tabataba’i rejects this because the next verse does not fit and “made” is not established to mean “named” in the cited passage.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بجعلهم أئمة يدعون إلى النار تسميتهم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Resurrection Day no intercession from any helper will reach them.
rows.anchor: وقوله { ويوم القيامة لا ينصرون } أي لا تنالهم شفاعة من ناصر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their lasting curse follows from their role as examples in disbelief: later followers’ sins continue to accrue to them, so the curse persists with their followers’ continuing unbelief and sins; the meaning is compared with God’s promise to believers.
rows.anchor: فهم لكونهم أئمة يقتدي بهم من خلفهم في الكفر والمعاصي لا يزال يتبعهم ضلال الكفر والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person given only worldly enjoyment is deprived of the good promise, as the contrast between the promise and temporary enjoyment indicates.
rows.anchor: وهو محروم من ذلك الوعد الحسن لاقتصاره على التمتع بمتاعها، والدليل على هذا التقييد المقابلة بين الوعد والتمتيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Brought forward” means either for punishment or questioning and accountability; thumma marks argumentative sequence, while the nominal sentence signals certainty, as does its parallel.
rows.anchor: أي للعذاب، أو للسؤال والمؤاخذة و { ثم } للترتيب الكلامي وإتيان الجملة اسمية كما فيما يقابلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supposed partners are those worshipped in worldly life; they count as partners because people attribute to them acts belonging to God, such as worship or governance, and “calling” them signals their distance and abandonment on that Day.
rows.anchor: الشركاء هم الذين كانوا يعبدونهم في الدنيا وكونهم شركاء عندهم لكونهم يعطونهم أو ينسبون إليهم بعض ما هو من شؤونه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged partners include honored servants such as angels and Jesus, rebellious jinn and humans claiming divinity such as Pharaoh and Nimrod, and false authorities such as Satan and leaders of misguidance.
rows.anchor: وصنف منهم كعتاة الجن ومدعي الألوهية من الإنس كفرعون ونمرود وغيرهما وقد ألحق الله سبحانه بهم كل مطاع في باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those saying they led others astray are the second group of alleged partners, the leaders from whom shirk and misguidance proceed; idolaters themselves also fall under the judgment, but this passage refers to those leaders.
rows.anchor: والذين يشير إليهم قوله { قال الذين حق عليهم القول } هم من الصنف الثاني بدليل ذكرهم إغواءهم وتبريهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their statement is included although the worshippers are not said to point them out, perhaps to show the worshippers have lost sight of them at this scene.
rows.anchor: وإيراد قول هؤلاء الشركاء مع عدم ذكر أن المسؤولين أشاروا إليهم لعله للإشارة إلى أنهم ضلوا عنهم في هذا الموقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disavowal is complete: the false partners had no power to compel the worshippers or deprive them of choice.
rows.anchor: وقوله { تبرأنا إليك } تبر منهم مطلقا حيث لم يكن لهم أن يلجؤهم ويسلبوا منهم الاختيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They did not worship us” can mean the worship was not compelled, or that the partners disown the acts so those acts are no longer attributed to them; Tabataba’i links the latter sense with other descriptions of the scene.
rows.anchor: أي بإلجاء منا، أو لتبرينا من أعمالهم فإن من تبرأ من عمل لم ينتسب إليه وإلى هذا المعنى يؤول قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A view says the partners mean the people worshipped their own desires or Satan instead; Tabataba’i calls this unsound.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى تبرأنا إليك من أعمالهم ما كانوا إيانا يعبدون بل كانوا يعبدون أهواءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two statements are not joined by a conjunction because each restates “we led them astray as we were astray.”
rows.anchor: ولكون كل من قوليه { تبرأنا إليك } { ما كانوا إيانا يعبدون } في معنى قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters call on supposed partners to save them and repel the punishment; the following mention of seeing the punishment clarifies the failed appeal.
rows.anchor: والمراد بدعوتهم دعوتهم إياهم لينصروهم ويدفعوا عنهم العذاب ولذا قال { ورأوا العذاب } بعد قوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reading supplies an omitted result: if they had been guided, they would have seen the punishment, meaning they would have recognized it as true.
rows.anchor: قيل جواب لو محذوف لدلالة الكلام عليه والتقدير لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون لرأوا العذاب أي اعتقدوا أن العذاب حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible reading takes “if only they had been guided” as a wish that they had been guided.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون لو للتمني أي ليتهم كانوا يهتدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After asking about partners and telling them to seek aid, God asks how they answered the messengers’ invitations to faith and good works.
rows.anchor: سئلوا أولا عن شركائهم وأمروا أن يستنصروهم، وثانيا عن جوابهم للمرسلين إليهم من عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blindness is a metaphor for inability to find an answer; attributing blindness to the reports rather than the people emphasizes every route is blocked and recourse cut off.
rows.anchor: العمى إستعارة عن جعل الإنسان بحيث لا يهتدي إلى خبر، وكان مقتضى الظاهر أن ينسب العمى إليهم لا إلى الأنباء

words: إن قارون كان من قوم موسى فبغى عليهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qarun narrative follows the polytheists’ fear that following guidance would get them driven from their land: his fate warns them that rejecting God leads to ruin and could befall them too.
rows.anchor: بيان قصة قارون من بني إسرائيل ذكرها الله سبحانه بعدما حكى قول المشركين { إن نتبع الهدى معك نتخطف من أرضنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun trusted his own skill, preferred worldly life, and pursued corruption; God sank him and his house, and no group could help or save him.
rows.anchor: فأمن العذاب الإلهي وآثر الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة وبغى الفساد في الأرض فخسف الله به وبداره الأرض

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines baghy as seeking unjust transgression or domination.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع البغي طلب العتو بغير حق

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ says mafātiḥ and mafātīḥ are plural forms with the same meaning: tools used to unlock things.
rows.anchor: قال والمفاتح جمع مفتح والمفاتيح جمع مفتاح ومعناهما واحد وهو عبارة عما يفتح به الأغلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes take the keys to mean Qarun’s treasure stores, but Tabataba’i rejects that interpretation.
rows.anchor: وذكر جمع من المفسرين أن المراد بالمفاتح الخزائن، وليس بذاك

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines nāʾa bi-ḥimlih as rising under a heavy burden.
rows.anchor: قال وناء بحمله ينوء نوءا إذا نهض به مع ثقله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another lexicographer says the load weighed its bearer down until it tilted him, which Tabataba’i finds more apt here.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره ناء به الحمل إذا أثقله حتى أماله وهو الأوفق للآية

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines ʿuṣba as a group whose members are closely bound together.
rows.anchor: وقال في المجمع أيضا العصبة الجماعة الملتف بعضها ببعض

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says ʿuṣba is a group of ten to fifteen people.
rows.anchor: فقيل ما بين عشرة إلى خمسة عشر عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says ʿuṣba is a group of ten to forty people.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما بين عشرة إلى أربعين عن قتادة

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says ʿuṣba means forty men.
rows.anchor: وقيل أربعون رجلا عن أبي صالح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ʿuṣba means a group of three to ten people.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما بين الثلاثة إلى العشرة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unattributed view defines ʿuṣba as a group whose members support one another.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنهم الجماعة يتعصب بعضهم لبعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s nine brothers call themselves ʿuṣba, undercutting the earlier estimates of ten to fifteen, ten to forty, or forty people.
rows.anchor: ويزيف غير القولين الأخيرين قول إخوة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejoicing means excessive worldly delight amounting to arrogant insolence; attachment to worldly pleasure distracts from the afterlife and breeds pride, which is why God does not love such people.
rows.anchor: فسر الفرح بالبطر وهو لازم الفرح والسرور المفرط بمتاع الدنيا فإنه لا يخلو من تعلق شديد بالدنيا ينسى الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on rejoicing is reinforced by the instruction not to exult over what God gave and that God loves no arrogant boaster.
rows.anchor: ولا تفرحوا بما آتاكم والله لا يحب كل مختال فخور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Use the worldly wealth God gave you to build the hereafter by spending it in God’s cause and in ways that please Him.
rows.anchor: أي واطلب فيما أعطاك الله من مال الدنيا تعمير الدار الآخرة بإنفاقه في سبيل الله ووضعه فيما فيه مرضاته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not neglect the share God allotted and provided; put it to work for the afterlife, since a person’s true share is what they do for the next life and what remains for them.
rows.anchor: أي لا تترك ما قسم الله لك ورزقك من الدنيا ترك المنسي واعمل فيه لآخرتك لأن حقيقة نصيب الإنسان من الدنيا هو ما يعمل به لآخرته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A view says one’s worldly share is small: enough food, drink, and clothing for oneself, leaving excess to others; Tabataba’i calls this good and says other views do not suit the context.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه لا تنس أن نصيبك من الدنيا - وقد أقبلت عليك - شيء قليل مما أوتيت وهو ما تأكله وتشربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spend on others in kindness as God kindly gave to you without your deserving it; this restates the first reading of worldly share or completes the second.
rows.anchor: أي أنفقه لغيرك إحسانا كما آتاكه الله إحسانا من غير ان تستحقه وتستوجبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not use wealth, status, or influence to seek corruption; God does not love corrupters because creation is grounded in goodness and reform.
rows.anchor: أي لا تطلب الفساد في الأرض بالاستعانة بما آتاك الله من مال وما اكتسبت به من جاه وحشمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun answers all the advice by denying his wealth was an undeserved divine favor and claiming he earned it through superior knowledge of acquiring and managing wealth; he therefore thinks he may use it for luxury, power, and ambition.
rows.anchor: وكان كلامهم مبنيا على أن ماله من الثروة إنما آتاه الله إحسانا إليه وفضلا منه من غير استيجاب واستحقاق فيجب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun’s self-crediting conceit is common among worldly people: they attribute wealth and power to their own ability, knowledge, and expertise, overlooking destiny and outward circumstances.
rows.anchor: لا يرى الواحد منهم فيما ساقه إليه التقدير ووافقته الأسباب الظاهرة من عزة عاجلة وقوة مستعارة إلا أن نفسه هي الفاعلة له
